story: Austin ordered security equipment for its parks and, in the same resolution, forbade its city manager from considering any camera or drone that depends upon artificial intelligence.

claims.text: The executed measure carries its resolution number and opens on a single whereas clause.
claims.quote: RESOLUTION NO. 20260812-017 WHEREAS ,
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The council states what it intends the measure to do, and the scanned text renders the word civil as eivil.
claims.quote: Austin City Council intends to invest in improving public safety and security in City parks while ensuring the protection ofeivil liberties;
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution directs the city manager to write a parks security implementation plan.
claims.quote: The City Manager is directed to develop a Parks Security Implementation Plan
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The plan has to rest on an audit the parks department already had done.
claims.quote: shall use the July 2025 Parks and Recreation Department Security Audit Findings and Recommendations Report
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution sets out what the plan has to establish.
claims.quote: planned operational and capital improvements, priority locations, responsible parties, funding mechanisms, and implementation timelines.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution names the equipment the city may buy.
claims.quote: The City Manager is directed to acquire, deploy, and activate equipment to improve parks security and safety, per the Security Audit, Implementation Plan, or both, potentially including but not limited to, security cameras, non-recording drones as first responders, lighting, access control/fencing/gates, signage and wayfinding, and radio communication systems.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: Whatever the city buys has to comply with the surveillance ordinance the council adopted in April.
claims.quote: Any surveillance technology sought must be acquired, deployed, and used in full compliance with all requirements of Ordinance No. 20260423-029, codified at City Code Chapter 2-19
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The prohibition opens by forbidding the city manager from even considering such a purchase, and the sentence runs off the foot of the first page at the word artificial.
claims.quote: The City Manager shall not consider acquisition of any camera or drone system that depends upon artificial
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The prohibition finishes at the top of the second page and names what the system must not be used for.
claims.quote: intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution says which parks get the equipment first.
claims.quote: Parks with a history of violent crime shall be prioritized for the initial deployment of this equipment.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution sets the date by which the city manager owes the council committee a progress update, and the scanned text drops the space after the comma in the date.
claims.quote: The City Manager shall provide a progress update on the direction given in this Resolution to the Council Climate, Water, Environment, and Parks Committee no later than December 9,2026.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution carries its adoption date.

claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

rejected.finding: the prohibition quoted as one contiguous sentence
rejected.reason: a page footer falls between the words artificial and intelligence in the document's text layer, so the sentence is carried as two claims rather than joined across the break

rejected.finding: a vote tally for the resolution
rejected.reason: the agenda page publishes no vote for the item and the city's own voting record dataset has loaded no meeting later than May 28th, 2026, so no tally was read on either

rejected.finding: the code library's text of City Code Chapter 2-19
rejected.reason: library.municode.com disallows this agent by name and returned 403. Not routed around. The ordinance text came from the city's own executed copy instead

rejected.finding: any statement in the resolution about artificial intelligence the city already runs, about enforcement, or about how depends upon artificial intelligence is to be judged
rejected.reason: the whole two page text was extracted and read and contains no such language. The silence is real and has no quotable string, so it is a note rather than a claim

rejected.finding: a count of the council members who sponsored the item
rejected.reason: counting them here would produce a numeral the document does not state

notes: Every quote was verified against a local extraction of the city's own PDFs made in this run, not against any third party reader.
The scanned text layer garbles the word civil as eivil in the whereas clause. The garbling is reported rather than repaired, and that clause is not set on a slide.

THE PROHIBITION IS NARROW AND MUST NOT BE OVERSTATED. It reaches a camera or drone system that depends upon artificial intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis. It is not a ban on artificial intelligence in Austin parks or in Austin city government.
It is written against future acquisition only, in the words shall not consider acquisition.
A resolution directs a manager. It is not an ordinance and it creates no offence.
The ordinance's text layer breaks the word of as o f in several places. That garbling is the scan's and is reproduced rather than repaired, so a quote can be searched for in the source.
